thread.title: Tech Today: Broadcom's Pledge, Autodesk's Metrics, iPhone X's Slump

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Broadcom's Pledge, Autodesk's Metrics, iPhone X's Slump
text:
Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
Shares of Broadcom ( AVGO ) are down $3.23, or 1.3%, at $247.73, this morning, after it issued a statement saying if it takes over Qualcomm ( QCOM ), it will "focus" the company's R&D efforts to "accelerate innovation and R&D," and to "create a stronger combined American company." The one-page release comes after Qualcomm's publication yesterday of a letter from the U.S. Treasury Department that cast aspersions upon Broadcom's style of business, claiming Broadcom takes a "private equity-style direction" that involves reducing investment.
In other Broadcom news, The New York Post 's Carleton English and Josh Kosman wrote late yesterday that Broadcom has told a Qualcomm shareholder the company is "accelerating its plans to re-domicile to the U.S.," intending to complete the change by sometime in April, versus an original expectations for "mid-May," without citing sources.
I would note that this morning's statement by Broadcom says "We are now in the final stages of redomiciling to the United States, and that process will be complete no later than May 6, 2018."
Qualcomm shares are down 20 cents at $61.95.
More bad news for iPhone
The parade of negatives about Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone , this one from Rosenblatt analyst Jun Zhang , who writes that the device "did not sell well during the Chinese New Year."
Zhang, who has a Buy rating on Apple shares, and a $180 price target, cuts his estimate for iPhone sales for the March quarter to 50 million from 52 million. He's holding onto an estimate for June of 38 million units, as he thinks the introduction of a version of the iPhone X in a red finish may offset the weak sales at the moment.
Part of this is some people "awaiting an expected 6.1-inch LCD iPh- one-a larger screen iPhone at a lower retail price," writes Zhang. But it's also further evidence "the high-end smartphone market upgrade cycle continues to extend."
Apple shares today are down $1.60, or 0.9%, at $175.07.
Autodesk's metrics
Shares of design software titan Autodesk ( ADSK ) are up $13.44, or 11%, at $133.31, after the company yesterday afternoon beat with its fiscal Q4 results, but missed with its forecast.
The lower outlook is not tempering enthusiasm, as price targets rise at several shops this morning.
Credit Suisse 's Michael Nemeroff , reiterating an Outperform rating, and rising his price target to $150 from $135, writes that it's all about " annualized recurring revenue ."
"We've been telling investors over the past few months to focus on ARR instead of subscribers, and we believe this quarter really drove that point home."
He thinks the most important part of the outlook is the forecast for ARR to rise by 28% to 30%, versus what has been consensus for 27.7%.
Take profit on Netflix
Shares of Netflix ( NFLX ) are down $3.40, or 1%, at $321.82, after Stifel Nicolaus 's Scott Devitt this morning cut his rating on the stock to Hold from Buy, even though he raises his price target to $325 from $283, writing that the share price " may have sprinted ahead of fundamentals in the short-term ."
"Netflix shares are up by nearly +70% YTD (versus the S&P 500 up +2% YTD), following a +55% move in 2017."
The downgrade follows several price target increases the last couple days .
Revitalizing Marvell
Shares of Marvell Technology Group (MRVL) are down a penny at $23.56, despite a very upbeat initiation of coverage by Argus Research 's Jim Kelleher , who starts the shares with a Buy rating, and a $28 price target, writing that Marvell's market opportunity is doubling as it acquires Cavium (CAVM). In the words of Kelleher, who has long covered Cavium, the deal will " revitalize Marvell ."
Ciena's diversification
Price targets are rising for fiber-optic networker Ciena (CIEN) after yesterday's fiscal Q1 beat and higher forecast revenue.
BMO Capital 's Tim Long , reiterating an Outperform rating, raises his target to $32 from $25, cheering the company's "diversification."
"Ciena's diversification strategy continues to pay off as non-telco sales now represent 35% of total revenue, with web-scale customers accounting for 15%," he writes. "The revenue contribution from web-scale is up 100% year-over-year, highlighting the impressive growth across the vertical."
Ciena shares are up 48 cents, or 1.9%, at $26.20, following a 10% jump yesterday.
Lam's bright prospects
Price targets are rising for chip equipment maker Lam Research (LRCX) after it held its annual analyst meeting in New York yesterday, during which it said it would more than double its dividend come June, add $2 billion to buybacks, and gave a forecast for fiscal 2021 of $23 to $25 per share in net income that was well above what some were expecting.
KeyBanc 's Weston Twigg , reiterating an Overweight rating, and raising his price target to $276 from $261, writing that "margins, cash generation, and shareholder returns should continue to expand meaningfully."
Lam shares are up 4 cents at $207.98.
Okta on tap
On tap for earnings this afternoon, after the closing bell, privacy and authentication management provider Okta (OKTA).
Okta stock is down 5 cents at $38.17.
